cards.title: Plan mode is dead

depth.text: someone built an **AI coding app** around plans, then found the **plans got in the way**

**Nuanced** had users discuss a feature, resolve ambiguities, then save a **persistent plan** before implementation; the author says the resulting **AI-written specs** were long and hard to read. He argues planning should stay part of a continuous loop of building, inspecting, and adjusting, rather than becoming a separate document.

cards.camps: Two camps: some say better models make a separate plan mode unnecessary; others say it still helps people understand changes and catch wrong assumptions.

comments.text: [I work on Claude Code] I broadly agree with the author’s point: plan mode was useful, and is no longer useful. In Claude Code, all plan mode does is add a little reminder to every user message along the lines of “you’re in plan mode, please don’t code yet”. It’s something I came up with late on a Sunday night many months ago, when I got tired of asking Claude to plan with me first before coding…

The real reason why plan mode is dead is because you can just conversationally instruct the agent to not make changes to the repository or to make changes to selected documents only, and it will listen. There was a time when we needed to enforce this via selected tool use, but we have surpassed that.

cards.title: Gravity seems holographic. What does that mean for reality?

depth.text: someone explores whether **gravity** lets a space’s **surface** describe what’s inside

In **AdS/CFT**, the gravitational interior of anti-de Sitter space is mathematically equivalent to a quantum theory on its boundary; black-hole entropy grows with **surface area, not volume**. Physicists disagree about whether that applies to **our universe** and what it would mean for reality.

cards.camps: Two camps: some commenters say the box analogy makes holography sound more mysterious than it is; others see it as a possible major shift, but say not to rush the coronation.

comments.text: Ok so imagine we set up two sets of babushca dolls. Each larger one has two smaller ones nested inside. The total mass of the two smaller ones between the two sets is equal in mass and they are configured to have the same centre of gravity. But crucially the individual masses of the inner dolls are different between the two sets. So maybe the innermost one is made of a denser material in set A…

Susskind's original paper is shockingly readable, at least the first section. It doesn't use a lot of fancy math or derivations to justify holography. Mostly it uses basic concepts from undergraduate physics to show how the idea of holography is consistent and makes sense, despite it seeming incredibly counterintuitive at first glance. For instance, figure 3 shows how you can't hide a black hole…

Pause for a moment to reflect on how outrageous this assertion is. You can’t see into the box at all. Nevertheless, holography says that you can learn exactly what’s happening everywhere in the box without any access to the interior. Observing the surface alone is enough. In this sense, the amount of stuff that fills a box is the same as the amount of paint that covers it. That’s a violation of…

Mathematician, not physicist, but it seems reasonable to me that you could encode a sufficiently constrained 3D space on a 2D boundary. And if you have such an encoding, it also doesn't seem insane that some things might be more easily modeled on the 2D boundary than the 3D space. If you can convert back and forth between a 2D representation and a 3D representation, and different phenomena are…

I think the box explanation is misleading. There isn't literally a box whose surface you measure. The idea is that the state of a higher-dimensional gravitational system can, in some cases, be completely described by a theory in one fewer dimension.

cards.title: One Piece of Flock Camera Data Put This Innocent Woman in Jail for 13 Days

depth.text: one **Flock camera sighting** helped police jail an innocent woman for **13 days**

Police linked Lindsey Isaacs’s **black Dodge Durango** to a fatal crash after a camera recorded it several miles away; witnesses described a **maroon Durango**, and hers had no damage. She spent **13 days in jail**, including 86 consecutive hours in solitary, before Florida dropped all charges in May 2026.

cards.camps: Two camps: some say Flock only supplied data and police caused the arrest; others say surveillance cameras make it easier for police to abuse data and skip basic checks.

cards.title: We're gonna need a lot more mathematicians

depth.text: someone argues **AI ideas** could outpace us, so we’ll need **more mathematicians** to understand them

Amit Sahai calls for **sustained support** for research groups to work through ideas produced by AI systems, arguing people need to understand the model and evidence behind consequential designs. His imagined **fusion plant** makes the stakes concrete: before approving construction, people should understand why it works and what justifies confidence in its safety.

glossary.GET request: A kind of web request that asks to fetch information, rather than send changes.
glossary.sandbox: A separate, contained space where software can be tested without affecting the rest of a computer or system.
glossary.payload: The piece of code or data a request carries or delivers.
glossary.link shortener: A service that turns a long web address into a shorter one.
glossary.API key: A secret code that lets software use an online service as an approved user.
glossary.Kubernetes: A system for running and managing software containers across computers.
glossary.cache poisoning: Tricking a system that saves copies into storing a fake one, so later users get it.
glossary.plan mode: A setting where a coding assistant is asked to work out what to do before it changes code.
glossary.spec: A written description of what a software feature should do.
glossary.agent: An AI system that can take steps and use tools to get a task done, not just answer questions.
glossary.codebase: The files and code that make up a software project.
glossary.harness: The surrounding code that gives an AI agent tools and a place to work, and checks what it does.
glossary.prompt cache: A saved copy of earlier instructions that a system can reuse instead of handling them again.
glossary.LLM: Large Language Model: an AI trained on lots of writing so it can take written questions and produce written answers.
glossary.PR: Pull request: a proposed code change shared so others can review it.
glossary.tokens: Small pieces of text an AI counts as it reads or writes; they can affect how much a request costs.
glossary.pathfinding: Working out how to get from one place to another.
glossary.AI: Artificial intelligence: computer systems designed to do tasks people associate with thinking.
glossary.Panopticon effect: A feeling that you may be watched at any time, so you change how you act even when you cannot tell whether anyone is watching.
glossary.data brokers: Companies that gather information about people and sell or share it with others.
glossary.force majeure: A contract term for extraordinary events outside someone’s control that may excuse them from carrying out their obligations.
glossary.SOFC: Solid oxide fuel cell: equipment that makes electricity from fuel through a chemical process.
glossary.liable: Legally responsible for something; a court can order the responsible party to pay for it.
glossary.data broker: A company that gathers information about people and sells or shares it.
glossary.targeted ads: Ads chosen for people based on information about them.
glossary.First Amendment: The part of the US Constitution that protects rights including freedom of speech.
glossary.AdS/CFT: Anti-de Sitter/conformal field theory correspondence: a mathematical match between gravity inside a special kind of space and a theory on its boundary.
glossary.conformal field theory: A kind of theory whose rules stay the same as you zoom in or out.
glossary.holographic principle: The idea that what happens inside a region of space can be fully described by information on its boundary.
glossary.entropy: A measure of how much stuff can fit inside an object.
glossary.entanglement: A quantum connection between particles, including particles on opposite sides of a boundary.
glossary.anti-de Sitter space: A kind of space that curves so its infinite expanse can be pictured inside a finite snow globe.
glossary.de Sitter space: A kind of space that curves outward, unlike the inward-curving space used in AdS/CFT.
glossary.qubit: A unit of quantum information, described here as a possible basic ingredient of reality.
glossary.it from qubit: A research idea that space is made from tiny units of quantum information.
glossary.ontology: The question of what is ultimately real, rather than just useful in a model.
glossary.OS: Operating system: the main software that runs a device and lets its apps work.
glossary.fixed-function application: A program made for one particular job, rather than one that can change to fit different requests.
glossary.BASIC: A programming language: a set of words and rules people use to tell a computer what to do.
glossary.container: A way to run a program in a separated space, limiting what it can access.
glossary.virtual machine: A computer-like environment made by software, used to run programs separately from the actual device.
glossary.array: A group of values treated together, rather than as separate items.
glossary.dynamic arrays: Spreadsheet formulas that can return several results, which Excel places into nearby cells.
glossary.spill: When a formula's results fill neighboring cells automatically.
glossary.index into: Pick a particular item from a group using its position.
glossary.probability distribution: A way to describe possible outcomes and how likely each one is.
glossary.ALPR: Automatic license plate recognition: technology that reads vehicle license plates from camera images.
glossary.solitary confinement: Being kept alone in a jail cell, apart from other people.
glossary.vehicular homicide: A criminal charge for causing someone’s death while driving.
glossary.human agency: People’s ability to make meaningful choices and shape what happens.
glossary.terawatt: A unit of power equal to one trillion watts.
glossary.formal proof: A proof written in strict rules so each step can be checked.
